title: Predict the output: a beginner code-reading quiz

questions.question: What does print(score) display?
questions.subject: computer-science
questions.hint: The old value is read before the new value is assigned.
questions.solution: score starts at 4, then 2 is added, so print(score) displays 6.
questions.explanation: An assignment replaces the variable value after the right-hand expression is calculated.
constraints: Trace the shown Python 3 code; it reads no input and has no external dependencies.
common_mistakes: Returning the initial value 4 or concatenating the digits as 42.

questions.question: How many times does the loop body run?
questions.subject: computer-science
questions.hint: Count the items in the sequence.
questions.solution: The list has three items and the loop body runs once for each item, so it runs three times.
questions.explanation: A for loop visits each list element once unless the body changes control flow; this body does not.
constraints: Trace the shown Python 3 code; it reads no input and has no external dependencies.
common_mistakes: Counting the starting index as an extra pass or stopping before the final list item.

questions.question: Which branch runs, represented by the printed word?
questions.subject: computer-science
questions.hint: Compare the two numbers before reading the branch.
questions.solution: Since 5 is greater than 3, the condition is true and the first branch prints true.
questions.explanation: The if body executes exactly when its comparison evaluates to True.
constraints: Trace the shown Python 3 code; compare the printed text case-insensitively.
common_mistakes: Reading else as the default branch without evaluating the comparison.

questions.question: What does print(values[0]) display?
questions.subject: computer-science
questions.hint: Python list indexes begin at zero.
questions.solution: Index 0 selects the first list item, which is 7.
questions.explanation: List positions start at zero, so values[0] refers to the first element.
constraints: Trace the shown Python 3 code; the list contains two integers.
common_mistakes: Treating index 0 as the second position or returning the index itself.
